real_gap.title: Where the work now sits — no longer a safety emergency, but two clean follow-ups
paragraphs: Yesterday's headline risk — 120 destinations (109 of them top-tier) showing no emergency contact at all — is resolved at the user-facing layer. The site now renders the national helplines (112 unified, 100 police, 101 fire, 102/108 ambulance, 1091 women, 1073 highway) on every sampled destination, and we verified this specifically on six pages that the database still records as having no curated local block (anjuna, bengaluru, betla, pattadakal, swamimalai, vishnuprayag). Those six rendered nothing yesterday and render the full helpline set today, so the universal fallback is live. No destination page is a dead end anymore.

What remains is content completeness, not safety. The database still has curated local emergency contacts (deep_dive.local_helpers) on 405 of 525 destinations and none on the other 120 — 109 of which are tier-A. Every one of the 405 curated blocks is clean: 867 phone entries, zero placeholders, zero free-text. The follow-up is to backfill curated district control-room and hospital numbers for those 109 tier-A destinations, at normal priority, from authoritative .gov.in/.nic.in sources — never fabricated. A small 'national helplines shown; local numbers being verified' label on fallback-only pages would set the right expectation in the meantime.

The second follow-up is the map. After 20 days fully absent it has started returning: 3 of the 10 sampled destinations (vishnuprayag, swamimalai, betla) now render a real tiled Leaflet map with no console errors, while the other 7 still show the decorative Atlas placeholder next to the (working) Places-to-Visit list. The remaining glitch is that even where the map renders, the location pins don't — 28-42 map tiles draw but 0 markers — so the POI coordinates already in the page payload still aren't plotted. Finishing the rollout to all destinations and fixing the empty pin layer closes this out.

risks: Map rollout is partial and the pin layer is empty where the map renders — a half-restored feature can read as broken; worth finishing or gating behind the cohort until pins work.

The 109 tier-A destinations still lean on generic national helplines rather than curated local numbers — fine as a floor, but a 'travel confidence' product should close this for its highest-traffic places.
